practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) established?
opts: Article 148
Article 152
Article 160
Article 280
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 148 of the Indian Constitution provides for an independent office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG). He is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the normal tenure of office for the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
opts: 4 years or up to the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier
5 years or up to the age of 60 years, whichever is earlier
6 years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
5 years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG holds office for a period of 6 years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier, as per Article 148.

practiceQuestions.q: Who appoints the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
opts: The Prime Minister of India
The President of India by warrant under his hand and seal
A collegium headed by the Chief Justice of India
Both Houses of Parliament through a joint resolution
practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG is appointed by the President of India by warrant under his hand and seal. This highlights the high constitutional status of the office.

practiceQuestions.q: By what process can the Comptroller and Auditor General of India be removed from office?
opts: By the President on the advice of the Prime Minister alone
In the same manner and on the same grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court
By a simple majority vote in Lok Sabha
At the pleasure of the President
practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG can be removed by the President only on an address from both Houses of Parliament supported by a special majority on the grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity, similar to a Supreme Court judge.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the CAG submit its audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union?
opts: The Prime Minister
The Speaker of Lok Sabha
The President of India
The Public Accounts Committee
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 151, the CAG submits audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union to the President, who shall cause them to be laid before each House of Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q: Which article of the Constitution mandates the submission of audit reports of the states by the CAG to the respective Governors?
opts: Article 149
Article 151
Article 165
Article 202
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 151(2) states that the audit reports of the CAG relating to the accounts of a state shall be submitted to the Governor of the state, who shall cause them to be laid before the legislature of the state.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a person who has served as CAG hold any further office under the Government of India or any state after retirement?
opts: Yes, with the permission of the Supreme Court
No, they are ineligible for any further office under the Government of India or of any state
Yes, they can be appointed as Governors immediately
Yes, after a cooling-off period of 3 years
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 148(4) clearly specifies that the CAG is not eligible for further office either under the Government of India or under the government of any state after he has ceased to hold his office.

practiceQuestions.q: Which parliamentary committee closely examines the audit reports submitted by the CAG?
opts: Estimates Committee
Committee on Public Undertakings
Public Accounts Committee (PAC)
Department-related Standing Committee on Finance
practiceQuestions.sol: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) examines the audit reports of the CAG relating to appropriation accounts and finance accounts of the Union, acting as a friend, philosopher, and guide to the CAG.

practiceQuestions.q: Who pays the salary and other service conditions expenses of the CAG?
opts: Contingency Fund of India
Consolidated Fund of India, charged upon it
Public Account of India
Divided equally between the Centre and States
practiceQuestions.sol: The administrative expenses of the office of the CAG, including all salaries, allowances, and pensions payable to or in respect of persons serving in that office, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 148(6).

practiceQuestions.q: Which duties and powers of the CAG are broadly outlined under Article 149 of the Constitution?
opts: The Constitution details every single auditing procedure in Article 149.
Article 149 empowers Parliament to prescribe duties and powers through legislation like the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.
The duties and powers are solely determined by executive executive order of the Cabinet.
The CAG has no statutory duties defined under Parliament acts.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 149 stipulates that the CAG shall perform such duties and exercise such powers in relation to the accounts of the Union and of the states as may be prescribed by or under any law made by Parliament. Consequently, Parliament enacted the CAG's (DPC) Act, 1971.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Comptroller and Auditor General of India often referred to as an 'agent of Parliament' rather than an executive officer?
opts: Because he is elected directly by the members of Parliament.
Because his primary constitutional function is to audit public expenditure on behalf of Parliament and ensure executive accountability to the legislature.
Because he can initiate legislation on financial matters in Parliament.
Because he is subordinate to the Public Accounts Committee in administrative matters.
practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG acts on behalf of Parliament to audit the accounts spent by the executive, ensuring that money is expended according to parliamentary appropriations. Thus, he functions as an instrument of parliamentary control over the executive.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the key structural difference between the CAG of India and the Comptroller General of the United States?
opts: The US Comptroller General performs both pre-audit and post-audit, whereas the Indian CAG mainly performs post-audit.
The Indian CAG has executive powers over government spending, while the US counterpart does not.
The Indian CAG is appointed by Parliament, whereas the US Comptroller General is appointed by the Governor.
There is no functional difference; both operate under identical statutes.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike in the UK or USA, the CAG of India has no control over the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund; the executive can draw money without the prior approval of the CAG. The Indian CAG's role is restricted to post-audit (auditing expenditure after it has been incurred).

practiceQuestions.q: How does the CAG ensure transparency and accountability in public-private partnerships (PPPs) or government-funded private bodies?
opts: The CAG has absolute jurisdiction to audit all private companies in India without exception.

Through specific statutory provisions, judicial pronouncements (such as the 2014 SC ruling on natural resources/private audits), and CAG's mandate to audit bodies substantially financed from public revenues.
By directly managing the board of directors of private companies receiving government grants.
The CAG is legally barred from inspecting any entity that has private equity participation.
practiceQuestions.sol: While the CAG's core mandate is government accounts, the Supreme Court and legislative amendments have reinforced that authorities or bodies substantially financed from public funds, including certain PPP projects and recipient trusts/societies, fall within the audit scope to maintain financial integrity.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of Performance Audits conducted by the CAG compared to traditional compliance and financial audits?
opts: Performance audit focuses only on arithmetic accuracy of vouchers.
It evaluates whether government programs, projects, and policies achieve their stated objectives with economy, efficiency, and effectiveness (the 3Es).
It replaces the judicial system by penalizing corrupt bureaucrats directly.
It is a mandatory daily audit report submitted directly to the Prime Minister's Office.
practiceQuestions.sol: Performance audit goes beyond verifying legal compliance and accounting accuracy. It assesses the '3Es'—Economy, Efficiency, and Effectiveness—examining whether public schemes achieve value for money and desired social outcomes.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Constitution separate the preparation of accounts from the auditing of accounts in the context of the Union government?
opts: To ensure absolute independence of the auditor from the accounting agency, preventing an auditor from auditing accounts compiled by themselves.
Because the CAG requested exemption from accounting duties due to staff shortages.
To allow the Reserve Bank of India to directly prepare all central ministry budgets.
To reduce the financial burden on the Consolidated Fund of India.
practiceQuestions.sol: In 1976, departmentalization of accounts was undertaken for the Union government, relieving the CAG of the responsibility of compiling accounts. This established the fundamental governance principle of 'no conflict of interest', separating the preparer of accounts from the independent auditor.

practiceQuestions.q: Consider the audit jurisdiction of the CAG regarding government companies. Which of the following best describes it?
opts: The CAG has no role in auditing government companies; only private statutory auditors do.
The CAG conducts supplementary audit of government companies whose accounts are first audited by private auditors appointed by the Central Government on the advice of CAG.
The CAG directly prepares the balance sheets of all Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs).
The CAG can liquidate any government company found financially unviable without cabinet approval.
practiceQuestions.sol: For government companies, commercial audit by the CAG involves supplementary audit. Private auditors appointed by the Central Government audit the accounts first, and then CAG can conduct a supplementary audit or issue comments under the Companies Act.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the independence of the CAG get safeguarded by its service conditions under the Indian Constitution?
opts: Its service conditions can be altered to its disadvantage after appointment by a simple majority vote.
Its salary and service conditions cannot be varied to its disadvantage after appointment.
The CAG can negotiate salary increments directly with the Ministry of Finance annually.
The CAG's tenure can be terminated by the cabinet whenever macroeconomic conditions worsen.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 148(3) states that the salary and other conditions of service of the CAG shall be such as may be determined by Parliament by law and shall not be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment, ensuring fearlessness in auditing.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional implication when the CAG submits its reports to the President or Governor?
opts: The reports become legally binding executive orders immediately upon submission.
The President or Governor is constitutionally bound to place them before the respective legislature for public scrutiny and debate.
The reports are kept confidential and classified under the Official Secrets Act.
The reports are sent directly to the Supreme Court for judicial prosecution.
practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG does not enforce compliance or penalize wrongdoers; its core constitutional function is transparency. By placing reports before Parliament or State Legislatures, it enables elected representatives to hold the executive accountable.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the role of the CAG critical in strengthening India's democratic framework of financial governance?
opts: Because it holds the executive financially accountable to the legislature and tax-paying citizens by checking misuse of public funds.
Because it dictates monetary policy rates in coordination with the Reserve Bank of India.
Because it drafts the Union budget every financial year.
Because it collects direct and indirect taxes across the country.
practiceQuestions.sol: Financial accountability is the bedrock of parliamentary democracy. The CAG acts as an independent watchdog ensuring that public resources authorized by Parliament are spent economically, efficiently, and legally, thereby upholding transparency.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies or authorities does the CAG NOT audit under its statutory authority?
opts: All trading, manufacturing, profit and loss accounts of Central and State governments
Local bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities) when recommended by the Finance Commission or state laws
Accounts of private corporate entities that have no government equity, no substantial financing, and no statutory audit mandate
All bodies and authorities substantially financed from Union or State revenues
All corporate authorities whose laws require audit by the CAG
practiceQuestions.sol: Purely private corporate entities with no government shareholding, no substantial government grants or financing, and no specific statutory requirement do not fall under the audit jurisdiction of the CAG.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG):
1. The CAG is mentioned in Part V of the Constitution under Chapter V (Articles 148-151).
2. The CAG is eligible for appointment to any other office under the Government of India after the expiry of his term if approved by the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The CAG office is provisioned in Chapter V of Part V of the Constitution (Articles 148-151). Statement 2 is incorrect because Article 148(4) explicitly bars the CAG from holding any further office under the Government of India or any state after retirement under any circumstance.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the duties and powers of the CAG:
1. The CAG audits all receipts and expenditure of the Consolidated Fund of India and of each state.
2. The CAG has statutory authority to audit the accounts of all corporations established by Parliament or State Legislatures.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Under Article 149 and the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the CAG audits receipts and expenditure from Consolidated Funds, Contingency Funds, Public Accounts, and corporations where law mandates CAG audit.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal and independence of the CAG:
1. The CAG can be removed by the President on grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity without any parliamentary resolution.
2. The expenses of the office of CAG, including all salaries and pensions, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because removal requires an address from both Houses of Parliament supported by a special majority, not solely executive action. Statement 2 is correct; expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, making them non-votable.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the three types of audit reports submitted by the CAG to the President:
1. Audit report on appropriation accounts
2. Audit report on finance accounts
3. Audit report on public undertakings
Which of these reports are examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC)?
opts: 1 and 2 only
3 only
1, 2 and 3
None of the above
practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG submits three audit reports to the President: audit reports on appropriation accounts, finance accounts, and public undertakings. All three reports are examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the auditing of government companies by the CAG:
1. The CAG directly appoints statutory auditors for all government companies without any consultation.
2. The CAG can conduct a supplementary audit of the financial statements of a government company.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because statutory auditors for government companies are appointed by the Central Government on the advice of the CAG, not directly by CAG. Statement 2 is correct; CAG can conduct a supplementary audit.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the accountability relationship between the CAG and the Legislature:
1. The CAG is accountable directly to the Supreme Court for all its audit findings.
2. The reports of the CAG provide the foundational material for parliamentary committees like the Public Accounts Committee to question ministers and bureaucrats.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect; CAG is an independent constitutional authority reporting to Parliament/State Legislature, not to the Supreme Court. Statement 2 is correct; PAC relies heavily on CAG reports.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the origin and evolution of the CAG office in India:
1. The office of the Auditor General was first created in British India in 1858 under Lord Canning.
2. The Government of India Act, 1919 gave statutory recognition to the audit independence of the Auditor General.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the first Auditor General was appointed in 1860 (under Lord Canning's administrative reforms after 1857). Statement 2 is correct; the Government of India Act, 1919 provided statutory recognition to the Auditor General's independence.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the CAG's jurisdiction over receipts and stores:
1. The CAG audits all receipts which flow into the Consolidated Fund of India to ensure that assessment and collection rules are properly framed.
2. The CAG has no mandate to audit the stock and stores of government offices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; the CAG audits tax and non-tax receipts to ensure proper collection. Statement 2 is incorrect because the CAG is explicitly empowered under the 1971 Act to audit and report on the stock and stores of all government offices and departments.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers of the CAG to call for records:
1. The CAG can inspect any office of accounts under the control of the Union or State governments, including records kept in electronic formats.
2. The CAG can demand any information, books, or papers necessary for audit, and government departments are legally required to provide them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct under the CAG's (DPC) Act, 1971. The CAG has sweeping powers to inspect offices, examine transactions, and demand records, ensuring complete transparency and access to information.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of CAG in auditing bodies and authorities:
1. The CAG audits the accounts of non-government bodies and NGOs only if they receive grants-in-aid above a specified threshold from the government, as stipulated by law or rules.
2. The CAG conducts audit of accounts of local bodies (Panchayats and Urban Local Bodies) automatically across all states under direct mandatory provisions of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; NGOs/bodies receiving government grants above specified limits can be subjected to CAG audit under sections 14 and 15 of the 1971 Act. Statement 2 is incorrect because CAG audit of local bodies is not automatically mandated directly by the Constitution for all states uniformly; it depends on state legislation, Governor's request, or recommendations of State Finance Commissions.
